Ch. 23 ἰαλτὸς ἐκ δόμων ἔβαν χοᾶν προπομπός [sent forth from the house I went as escort of the libations].
Προπομποί [Escorts] was the title of a tragedy of Aeschylus (fr. 267).
Thus Casaubon instead of χοὰς πρόπομπος [escort of the libations] (for this is the accent in M).
We will go and bury him, these escorts

Propontis, the sea which is before the Euxine Pontus, adjacent to Byzantium: concerning this name and its relation to the name Ἑλλησπόντου [Hellespont] see the passages of writers collected in Thes. vol. 6 p. 1822. On both most recently G. Gebhardt has spoken (Blätter für das Bayerische Gymnasialwesen vol. 2 fasc. 7 p. 389-399.).

Thus corrected by the meter instead of μορσίμου βρόχου τυχεῖν ἐν ἀρτάναις [to obtain the fateful noose in the halter], which, since ἀρτάναις [halters] is scanned, either μορσίμου λάχους [fateful lot] or θανασίμου βρόχου [deadly noose] must be said: on which see the Preface to the Leipzig edition of Aeschylus, fifth, p. LXXII. The adverb προπρό [before] is used by Apollonius Rhodius: among the tragic poets it is not read elsewhere than πρόπαρ [before], which Aeschylus says a little later at v. 791.
